subject: Eval setup and scoring criteria for FinTech Co - next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Jessica Liu <jessica.liu@fintechco.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@fintechco.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Mar 2026 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Eval setup + recommended models for FinTech Co

Hi Jessica / Marcus —

Thanks again for the productive discovery call this morning. Recap + proposed next steps to get the customer-specific evals running on Redwood:

1) Goal: validate model fit on your anonymized ticket dataset for three intents (payment issue, account access, dispute) and measure quality regression risk vs your current rule-based baseline.

2) Recommended model candidates for the eval run (we'll surface latency/cost tradeoffs):
   - Llama-2-Chat-70B (8-bit quantized) — best quality baseline for broad conversational understanding.
   - RedLite-13B (optimized, quantized) — lower-cost option for latency-sensitive routes.
   - Redwood-moderate-7B (fast, smaller footprint) — useful for defensive fallbacks.

3) Benchmark artifacts and prompt sets: attached example prompt_set.csv (one-shot + zero-shot prompts we discussed) and a small dataset sample (fintech-eval-dataset-sample.csv).

4) Dataset format & required columns (easy to validate):
   - CSV UTF-8, newline-delimited
   - Columns: id, input_text, expected_response, category, priority
   - For multi-turn contexts include a context field (optional) where messages are concatenated with delimiters.

5) Scoring criteria (what we'll run by default):
   - Automated metrics: semantic similarity (embedding cosine) + ROUGE-L for short responses.
   - Discrete checks: intent match (boolean), entity extraction F1 for required slots.
   - Human review: we recommend a 200-sample human eval stratified by category to catch subtle regressions. See attached scoring-rubric.pdf for the rubric.

6) Execution plan & timeline:
   - Step A (this week): FinTech Co provides a 500-row sample in the sample CSV format + any sensitive-data notes.
   - Step B (next week): Redwood runs a smoke eval on 500 rows across the three model candidates and shares a quality + cost matrix.
   - Step C (week after): iterate prompts, run 5k-row pilot, and then scale.

7) Access & artifacts: please share a secure Drive or S3 link for the dataset (we can accept temporary presigned URLs). We'll store artifacts in a customer-scoped evaluation workspace and share the evaluation dashboard link.

Attachments included: fintech-eval-dataset-sample.csv, prompt_set.csv, scoring-rubric.pdf, mutual-action-plan.xlsx

If that plan looks good, confirm the dataset link and whether you prefer Redwood to run the smoke eval (we'll do it under FT-2026-0042). Rishi will loop in on the technical bits.

Best,
Marissa

Hi Jessica — quick answers from the SE side.

1) Timeline: If you upload a 500-row sample by EOD, we can run the smoke eval within 24-48 hours. We typically do a parallel run across the three candidate models and produce the cost/latency/quality matrix the next day.

2) Local runs: you can run a functional smoke test locally (we'll provide a Dockerized harness), but exact parity requires Redwood runtime for consistent batching, KV-cache behavior, and quantized kernel choices. For model-comparison numbers we recommend letting Redwood run the official smoke eval (we'll share raw outputs so you can reproduce locally if needed).

3) Dataset validation rules (please validate before upload):
   - CSV must be UTF-8, no BOM, newline-terminated
   - id must be unique strings
   - expected_response should be the canonical target (trim whitespace, avoid markup)
   - if there are PII concerns, please flag rows in a pii_flag column; we can redact during processing

4) Eval config (what we'll run by default):
   - sample_size: 500
   - metrics: [semantic_similarity_embedding, rouge_l, intent_match_boolean, slot_f1]
   - pass_thresholds: semantic_similarity >= 0.75 OR intent_match == true for category-level pass

5) Attachments & artifacts: I've attached prompt_set.csv (examples we discussed) and scoring-rubric.pdf. We also uploaded a draft mutual-action-plan to the linked Drive folder.

Cost note: A 500-row smoke eval across the 70B quantized model typically costs in the low hundreds of USD (estimate depends on avg token count). We'll provide an exact estimate after we inspect average tokens per input.

Happy to set up a 30-min technical runbook session with your ML infra team — available Tue/Wed next week.

-Rishi
